children: According to CNBC, President Donald Trump and senior administration officials have mounted a public campaign to stop the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates at its Sept. 15-16 meeting, with Trump threatening to halt trade with countries that run surpluses with the U.S. unless the Fed cuts rates. Vice President JD Vance said the Fed should be lowering rates, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a CNBC interview that the central bank typically does not raise rates during a supply shock until second- or third-order inflation effects emerge. Markets are pricing in about a 60% probability of a rate hike, helped by a strong jobs report Friday, and the administration has pointed to a three-month annualized core CPI rate of 1.6% versus just over 3% for the three-month annualized core PCE price index. Fed officials have said the Friday CPI report will be a key gauge of whether inflation is easing or still accelerating.

title: Trump Administration Pressures Fed To Avoid Rate Hike Ahead Of September Meeting
